main_body: Marble column: a tall shaft (rows 17-39) with a wider capital (rows 9-15) and base (rows 41-47), each drawn as a flat rectangular block
top_band: Capital top: white/very light grey, rows 10-11 (about 2-3 rows). It is a flat rectangular band with no ellipse and no visible cut face. The shaft top is hidden behind the capital.
evidence: The capital and base are straight-on horizontal bands, like the red 'flat band cap' guide. The light band at the top is only 2-3 rows, and it reads as a lit rim on a front-facing block rather than a foreshortened ellipse like the green guide column. There is no distinct front-edge line, and the cap's dark underside only separates it from the shaft. The shaft is a vertical gradient strip seen face-on. The top end shows no real top surface or cut face, so this is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The shaft is a smooth vertical grey gradient of about 4 steps, with no grain, veining, chips or speckle. The capital and base are large flat white and grey fills. The outline is a dark purple-grey on the left and bottom and is absent elsewhere, so it is only partly tinted. Next to the cheese stall and well, which have per-tile highlights and grain, most tiles here carry only 3-4 colours. The piece looks thinner and flatter than the references.
